title:
Know what's
actually there.
body: Scan it, add it, move on. Pantry should be the kitchen's current state, not another list you have to babysit.
points: Kitchen Scan feeds the pantry instead of dying as a one-off result.
Quantities, categories and storage state become useful context.
Everything downstream can ask the same question: what is actually here?

title:
Use it before
it becomes a problem.
body: A date alone is not freshness. 4DK keeps track of what the date means, how the food is stored, what happened to it and how certain the answer is.
points: Fresh, Use Soon, Priority and Check are useful states, not fake certainty.
Package dates, purchase dates, opened/cooked/frozen events stay distinct.
Freshness can change what gets recommended tonight.

title:
Ask from the kitchen
you actually have.
body: You should not have to explain your pantry, your preferences and what you ate yesterday every time you ask a food question.
points: Ask reads current kitchen state before answering.
Freshness, people, location and recent meals can change the answer.
The goal is fewer random suggestions and less re-explaining yourself.

title:
Saw it?
Bring it home.
body: A recipe you found somewhere else should not stay a bookmark. STEAL IT turns it into something 4DK can actually reason about.
points: Import from supported links, images or text.
Normalize ingredients and compare them against your kitchen.
Keep the version that actually worked when you cook it.
note: steal the idea. keep your version.

title:
Everybody eats
different.
body: One kitchen can belong to several people without pretending everyone has the same taste, restrictions or history.
points: Shared kitchen state stays shared.
Individual preferences stay individual.
Recommendations can optimize for who is actually eating.

title:
A week should not
feel like seven resets.
body: Turn the food you already have and the meals that make sense into an actual week instead of planning in a vacuum.
points: Plans can start from pantry and freshness, not a blank calendar.
Recent meals help keep repetition under control.
The shopping list can inherit what the plan is actually missing.

title:
Buy what's missing.
Not what you already own.
body: Shopping should close the gap between the plan and the pantry, not create another disconnected list.
points: Pantry coverage separates what you own from what you need.
Planned meals can add missing ingredients automatically.
Later retail integrations can plug into the same shopping state.

title:
Next time should
start smarter.
body: If you changed a recipe and liked it, cooked something yesterday or keep rejecting the same ingredient, that should matter later.
points: Explicit preferences stay separate from observed behaviour.
Useful adaptations can be retrieved instead of recalculated.
Recent meals, history and successful changes give the next decision context.
